## Reproduction

The agent's work, under my direction. The full agent report (rendered from the course's `reproducibilityReport.Rmd`) is in [`agent_report/`](agent_report/reproducibilityReport.Rmd). The code below is the same analysis.

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(car)        # Type III sums of squares
library(effectsize) # partial eta squared
library(knitr)
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))  # needed for meaningful Type III tests
```

```{r}
#| label: load
d_raw <- read_excel("data/S1_Subway.xlsx")
glimpse(d_raw)
```

```{r}
#| label: preprocess
# The paper's factor is "orientation (toward vs. away from the rated station)".
# The data only has travel direction, so orientation = f(direction, station):
# westbound -> toward Spadina/St. George, away from Bloor-Yonge/Sherbourne; eastbound -> reverse.
d <- d_raw |>
  mutate(
    station   = factor(STN_NAME, levels = c("SPAD", "STG", "B-Y", "SHER"),
                       labels = c("Spadina", "St. George", "Bloor-Yonge", "Sherbourne")),
    direction = factor(DIRECTION, levels = c("WEST", "EAST")),
    orientation = factor(
      ifelse((DIRECTION == "WEST" & STN_NUMBER %in% 1:2) |
             (DIRECTION == "EAST" & STN_NUMBER %in% 3:4), "toward", "away"),
      levels = c("toward", "away"))
  )

nrow(d)                         # paper: 202
table(d$direction)              # paper: 101 / 101
table(d$direction, d$station)   # unbalanced: Bloor-Yonge n = 49

d |>
  group_by(station, direction) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(DISTANCE), se = sd(DISTANCE) / sqrt(n), .groups = "drop") |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Cell means (cf. Figure 1)")
```

```{r}
#| label: analysis
# (a) As described in the paper: orientation (toward/away) x station
m_orient <- lm(DISTANCE ~ orientation * station, data = d)
a_orient <- Anova(m_orient, type = 3)
a_orient
eta_squared(a_orient, partial = TRUE)

# (b) Travel direction (east/west) x station
m_dir <- lm(DISTANCE ~ direction * station, data = d)
a_dir <- Anova(m_dir, type = 3)
a_dir
eta_squared(a_dir, partial = TRUE)

# Station F depends on SS type with unbalanced cells:
Anova(m_dir, type = 2)["station", ]

# Per-station east vs. west tests (separate one-way ANOVAs)
per_station <- map_dfr(c("St. George", "Spadina", "Bloor-Yonge", "Sherbourne"), function(stn) {
  ds <- filter(d, station == stn)
  s  <- summary(aov(DISTANCE ~ direction, data = ds))[[1]]
  tibble(station = stn,
         M_west = mean(ds$DISTANCE[ds$direction == "WEST"]),
         M_east = mean(ds$DISTANCE[ds$direction == "EAST"]),
         F = s$`F value`[1], df = paste(s$Df, collapse = ", "),
         p = s$`Pr(>F)`[1],
         eta2p = s$`Sum Sq`[1] / sum(s$`Sum Sq`))
})
kable(per_station, digits = 4)
```

**Agent's summary of values** (from the output above):

| 2 | F = 24.10, ηp² = .27 | F = 24.10, ηp² = .27 | F = 24.10, ηp² = .27 (Type II: 23.35) |
| 3 | F = 16.28, ηp² = .20 | F = 0.93, p = .43, ηp² = .01 | F = 16.28, ηp² = .20 |
| 4 | St. George p \< .001, ηp² = .28 |  | F(1,49) = 18.79, p = .0001, ηp² = .277 |
| 5 | Spadina p = .001, ηp² = .20 |  | F(1,49) = 11.97, p = .0011, ηp² = .196 |
| 6 | Bloor-Yonge p = .053, ηp² = .08 |  | F(1,47) = 3.95, p = .0528, ηp² = .077 |

## Checker's verdict

Filled in by you, not the agent.

| \# | Paper value | Reproduced value | Verdict (exact / minor / major / not reproducible) | Reason for discrepancy |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| 1 | F \< 1 | F(1,194) = 46.00, ηp² = .19 | Major | The main effect and interaction flip. The papers description doesnt match what was computed. with toward/away coding, orientation has a *large* main effect (F = 46.00) instead of F \< 1. If you code the factor as east/west travel direction, you get F = 0.32, which matches the paper. So the authors appear to have analyzed direction, not orientation. |
| 2 | F(3, 194) = 24.10, ηp² = .27 | F = 24.10, ηp² = .27 | Exact | matches as the paper describes. |
| 3 | F(3, 194) = 16.28, ηp² = .20 | F = 0.93, p = .43, ηp² = .01 | Major | with toward/away coding, the interaction *disappears* (F = 0.93, p = .43). With east/west coding it's F = 16.28, ηp² = .20, an exact match. Same cause as row 1. |
| 4 | p \< .001, ηp² = .28 | p = .0001, ηp² = .277 | Exact | matches as the paper describes ( they do round) |
| 5 | p = .001, ηp² = .20 | p = .0011, ηp² = .196 | Exact | matches as the paper describes ( they do round) |
| 6 | p = .053, ηp² = .08 | p = .0528, ηp² = .077 | Exact | matches as the paper describes ( they do round) |
| 7 | p \< .001, ηp² = .24 | p = .0003, ηp² = .236 | Exact | matches as the paper describes ( they do round) |

Agent's own claim about success, and whether it was right:

*Agent's claim:* All seven target values reproduce exactly, but only when the between-subjects factor is coded as travel direction (east/west) rather than orientation (toward/away), and only with Type III SS. Coded as the paper describes it, outcomes 1 and 3 do not reproduce: the orientation main effect is large and the interaction is null. The agent concluded that the paper mislabels the analysis it ran, and that the substantive conclusion is unchanged.

*Was it right?*

Yes I belive the agent was correct. Looing at the paper, I can see that the what the authors descibe they did versus what they calcuate did not match, and the agent was able to figure this out on its own which was very well done.
